product_brief: Smart card system supporting hybrid PQC and current public-key cryptography for secure authentication.
pqc_capability_description: Supports hybrid methodology using ML-DSA (NIST standard) and ECDSA. Firmware developed by ISARA. Tested on H-LINCOS testbed. Targeting full-scale deployment in 2030, with limited practical implementations planned for 2025.
key_management_model: Smart card-based hardware key storage with hybrid certificate support.
primary_platforms: Smart cards, H-LINCOS (Healthcare Long-term INtegrity and Confidentiality protection System)
pqc_roadmap_details: Limited practical implementations in 2025 in healthcare and financial sectors; full-scale deployment targeting 2030.
authoritative_source_url: https://www.holdings.toppan.com/en/news/2024/10/newsrelease241007_1.html (inferred from source context, though exact URL not explicitly in text body, source file name suggests toppan-securebridge-hpki-pqc-8339ff4a.html)
testing_&_validation_methods: Pilot testing on H-LINCOS quantum cryptography network testbed (April to September 2024) to confirm basic functionality and user authentication.
qkd_protocols_&_quantum_networking: Tested on a quantum cryptography network testbed operated by NICT; H-LINCOS uses quantum cryptography.
deployment_&_migration_complexity: Hybrid methodology allows smooth transition; supports systems at various stages of PQC migration.

product_brief: A demonstrator for Germany's next-generation national ID card combining classical and post-quantum cryptography on Infineon chips.
pqc_capability_description: A functional proof-of-concept demonstrator for a national ID card that combines classical and post-quantum cryptography. It implements quantum-resistant digital signature schemes for personal data protection and covers both encryption and authentication. The implementation is on specialized Infineon chips featuring a new design for fast, side-channel-resistant software implementation of PQC algorithms.
key_management_model: Hardware key storage on specialized Infineon chips; secure key generation and injection methods not explicitly detailed beyond chip implementation.
architecture_type: Smart card/ID card form factor using specialized Infineon chips.
primary_platforms: Germany’s national ID card infrastructure; Infineon chips.
regulatory_status: Developed in collaboration with the German Federal Office for Information Security (BSI); aligns with BSI recommendations and EU roadmap for PQC adoption by 2030.
pqc_roadmap_details: Germany’s transition to quantum-secure ID cards will occur in two stages: first, protecting personal data from forgery using a quantum-resistant digital signature scheme; second, a full transition to quantum-secure technology. EU roadmap calls for PQC adoption in critical applications by 2030.
signature_schemes: Quantum-resistant digital signature scheme (specific algorithm name not stated); classical signature schemes implied but not named.
implementation_attack_surface: The Infineon chips feature a new design that supports fast, side-channel-resistant software implementation of PQC algorithms.
constrained_device_&_iot_suitability: Designed for ID card chips; addresses the technical challenge of minimizing the computational footprint of resource-intensive PQC algorithms on these constrained devices.
supply_chain_&_vendor_risk: Developed by Giesecke+Devrient and Bundesdruckerei using chips from semiconductor manufacturer Infineon.
deployment_&_migration_complexity: Transition occurs in two stages; involves integrating PQC algorithms into national identity documents while meeting new security requirements.

product_brief: Smart card system integrated with secondary root certificates for secure migration to post-quantum cryptography.
pqc_capability_description: Successfully completed a proof of concept (PoC) demonstrating smooth transition from existing certificate authentication infrastructure to PQC. Integrated with a secondary crypto-agile root certificate on a quantum cryptography network testbed. Supports ML-DSA (a NIST-standardized PQC algorithm) alongside current cryptographic methods for smart card-based ID verification.
key_management_model: Smart card-based key storage; integrated with secondary crypto-agile root certificate for certificate issuance.
primary_platforms: Quantum cryptography network testbed (developed by NICT)
pqc_roadmap_details: PoC completed in April 2026; partners to share details at Quantum Computing Expo Tokyo (April 15-17, 2026). Project requested by Japan’s Cross-ministerial Strategic Innovation Promotion Program (SIP).
testing_&_validation_methods: Proof of Concept (PoC) on a quantum cryptography network testbed; simulated transition phase testing.
constrained_device_&_iot_suitability: Smart card form factor used for ID verification and internet access.
supply_chain_&_vendor_risk: Partnership between Toppan Holdings, NICT, and Isara Corporation.
deployment_&_migration_complexity: Designed to avoid transition phase with service disruptions or outages; demonstrated smooth transition in simulated phase.
